assessments.reasoning: Capture 038a217603514c75a96f9c4c3d4beef8 is W3C’s English versioned software-license page. Its full digest matches the claim revision and both cited ranges agree. The page title, self-link, conditional copying, modification and distribution grant, and change history establish the 2002 publisher identity.

The Index’s commit-pinned taxonomy in capture 9e608fc932dd477596eabdff200ae980 matches the cited admission range. The 2002 software grant has an identifiable text and edition under W3C’s authority, which fits License. The separately linked short notice and document license do not change the classification.

challenge.method: Compared the heading, 'This version' and 'Latest version' links, operative grant, archive banner, activation paragraph and separately listed 2002 document-license route.
challenge.results: W3C explicitly distinguishes /copyright/document-license-2002/ from the selected software-license page. The latter describes the prior 1998 formulation and its removal of the ambiguous grant of 'use'. W3C gives December 31, 2002 as activation. The SPDX December 13 release note supplies no basis for changing that finding.

limitations: Active expresses the intended Index lifecycle mapping. W3C records a revised and renamed successor adopted May 13, 2015. Current admission, first publication, rights for a particular project, redistribution of the reference text and installation eligibility remain separate questions.
reasoning: W3C’s English /copyright/software-license-2002/ page identifies this version, states its activation and grants conditional permission for software and its documentation. The captured page title is 'Software and Document license - 2002 version'. The claim’s 'W3C Software Notice and License (2002 edition)' serves as the Index name. SCES §§1, 3 and 6 require the reviewer to resolve differences in terminology against the controlling source and exact edition. The versioned route, grant and history identify the instrument despite the title difference.
